about: Rogue Trader starting points for the pedalboard. Each recipe is an existing scenario in scenarios.json (base) plus settings to add or override (set); keys are the flat control keys scenarios.json uses (Faust shortname form of the control label). These are starting points to tune by ear against the game voices in the FX Lab monitor, not finished sounds. The Pasqal recipe aims at what the game's own Pasqal clips measure: left/right correlation about 0.77, side/mid about -9 dB, the two sides differing mostly below 300 Hz, level difference swinging about 2.5 dB at about 1 Hz.

recipes.name: RT Tech-priest (Pasqal target, stereo)
recipes.desc: Mid scoop and weight at the bottom like the game's Pasqal, a little metal ring, and a bass band that differs between the ears and moves.

recipes.name: RT Servitor (flat buzz, drifting)
recipes.desc: The flat Dalek-style drone with a slow drift between the ears and a low band that wanders.

recipes.name: RT Machine spirit (inharmonic)
recipes.desc: Frequency-shifted partials, a metal-bar ring and a hollow comb, with the two sides phasing slowly against each other.

recipes.name: RT Vox-caster (field radio, light width)
recipes.desc: The field radio with the faintest left/right movement so it does not sit dead centre.

recipes.name: RT Helmet (Astartes, small width)
recipes.desc: Sealed helmet voice with a touch of stereo chorus for the room inside the helmet.

recipes.name: RT Ghost / psyker (wide)
recipes.desc: A doubled, drifting voice that moves between the ears, with a slow phase sweep that differs per side.

recipes.name: RT Daemon (layered, wide)
recipes.desc: The layered daemon with its low layer swinging between the ears.

recipes.name: RT Necron (cold, wide)
recipes.desc: Cold ancient voice with a little downward frequency shift, a metal ring and a slow wide phase.

recipes.name: RT Aeldari (subtle, airy)
recipes.desc: Restrained: a little stereo chorus and the faintest slow pan.

recipes.name: RT Trazyn projection (flicker)
recipes.desc: A failing projection: the failing-recording chain with sides that phase against each other and a quick flutter of the pan.
